sanskrit: taṃ cen mṛtyuḥ sarvaharo 'bhirakṣet; sadāpramattaḥ samare kirīṭinam tathāpi hantāsmi sametya saṃkhye; yāsyāmi vā bhīṣmapathā yamāya
english: Even if Death himself, who carries off all, should guard that crowned one—Kirīṭin—ever-watchful in the fray, even then I shall slay him when we close in battle, or else I shall go to Yama by the road Bhīṣma has taken.

sanskrit: na tv evāhaṃ na gamiṣyāmi teṣāṃ; madhye śūrāṇāṃ tat tathāhaṃ bravīmi mitradruho durbalabhaktayo ye; pāpātmāno na mamaite sahāyāḥ
english: Yet I will surely go into the midst of those heroes—this I declare as it is. But those who betray their friends, whose loyalty is feeble, those evil-souled men—they are no comrades of mine.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca sa siddhimantaṃ ratham uttamaṃ dṛḍhaṃ; sakūbaraṃ hemapariṣkṛtaṃ śubham patākinaṃ vātajavair hayottamair; yuktaṃ samāsthāya yayau jayāya
english: Saṃjaya said: Mounting his splendid, sturdy, well-equipped chariot—its pole adorned, wrought with gold, fair to see, crowned with a banner and yoked to the finest horses swift as the wind—he set forth to victory.

sanskrit: saṃpūjyamānaḥ kurubhir mahātmā; ratharṣabhaḥ pāṇḍuravājiyātā yayau tadāyodhanam ugradhanvā; yatrāvasānaṃ bharatarṣabhasya
english: Honored by the Kurus, that great-souled bull among charioteers, drawn by pale steeds, the fierce-bowed warrior, went forth then to the battleground, to where the bull of the Bharatas had met his end.

sanskrit: varūthinā mahatā sadhvajena; suvarṇamuktāmaṇivajraśālinā sadaśvayuktena rathena karṇo; meghasvanenārka ivāmitaujāḥ
english: In a chariot great and armored, with its banner, gleaming with gold and pearls and gems and diamonds, yoked to noble horses and thundering like a cloud, Karṇa rode—measureless in might, like the sun itself.

sanskrit: hutāśanābhaḥ sa hutāśanaprabhe; śubhaḥ śubhe vai svarathe dhanurdharaḥ sthito rarājādhirathir mahārathaḥ; svayaṃ vimāne surarāḍ iva sthitaḥ
english: Bright as the fire-eater, in his fire-bright, fair chariot the radiant bowman stood—Adhiratha's son, that mighty car-warrior, shining as he stood, like the king of the gods himself stationed in his celestial car.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca śaratalpe mahātmānaṃ śayānam amitaujasam mahāvātasamūhena samudram iva śoṣitam
english: Saṃjaya said: That great-souled one of boundless might lay upon his bed of arrows, like the ocean drained dry by a vast gathering of winds.

sanskrit: divyair astrair maheṣvāsaṃ pātitaṃ savyasācinā jayāśāṃ tava putrāṇāṃ saṃbhagnāṃ śarma varma ca
english: That great archer, felled by Savyasācin with celestial weapons—and with him the hope of victory of your sons, their shelter and their armor, all shattered.

sanskrit: apārāṇām iva dvīpam agādhe gādham icchatām srotasā yāmuneneva śaraugheṇa pariplutam
english: He who had been like an island in a shoreless deep to men longing for footing in the fathomless waters—now flooded over by a torrent of arrows as by the current of the Yamunā.

sanskrit: mahāntam iva mainākam asahyaṃ bhuvi pātitam nabhaścyutam ivādityaṃ patitaṃ dharaṇītale
english: Like the great Maināka mountain, unbearable, cast down upon the earth; like the sun fallen from the sky, lying upon the ground.

sanskrit: śatakrator ivācintyaṃ purā vṛtreṇa nirjayam mohanaṃ sarvasainyasya yudhi bhīṣmasya pātanam
english: Unthinkable, like the defeat of Śatakratu by Vṛtra in olden days—the felling of Bhīṣma in battle, a thing to daze the whole army.

sanskrit: kakudaṃ sarvasainyānāṃ lakṣma sarvadhanuṣmatām dhanaṃjayaśaravyāptaṃ pitaraṃ te mahāvratam
english: The crest of all the armies, the very emblem of all bowmen, pierced through by Dhanaṃjaya's shafts—your father, the man of the great vow.

sanskrit: taṃ vīraśayane vīraṃ śayānaṃ puruṣarṣabham bhīṣmam ādhirathir dṛṣṭvā bharatānām amadhyamam
english: When Adhiratha's son beheld that hero lying upon the bed of heroes, that bull among men, Bhīṣma, peerless among the Bharatas—

sanskrit: avatīrya rathād ārto bāṣpavyākulitākṣaram abhivādyāñjaliṃ baddhvā vandamāno 'bhyabhāṣata
english: —he stepped down from his chariot, stricken, his voice broken with tears, and saluting him, his palms joined in reverence, spoke in homage.

sanskrit: karṇo 'ham asmi bhadraṃ te adya mā vada bhārata puṇyayā kṣemayā vācā cakṣuṣā cāvalokaya
english: "I am Karṇa—blessings be upon you! Speak to me today, O Bhārata; look upon me with a kind and gracious word, and with your eyes."

sanskrit: na nūnaṃ sukṛtasyeha phalaṃ kaś cit samaśnute yatra dharmaparo vṛddhaḥ śete bhuvi bhavān iha
english: "Surely no one in this world reaps the fruit of his good deeds, when you—aged, devoted to dharma—lie here upon the bare earth."

sanskrit: kośasaṃjanane mantre vyūhapraharaṇeṣu ca nātham anyaṃ na paśyāmi kurūṇāṃ kurusattama
english: "In raising up a treasury, in counsel, in battle-arrays and in the wielding of weapons, I see no other protector for the Kurus, O best of the Kurus."

sanskrit: buddhyā viśuddhayā yukto yaḥ kurūṃs tārayed bhayāt yodhāṃs tvam aplave hitvā pitṛlokaṃ gamiṣyasi
english: "You, endowed with a clear and stainless mind, who could carry the Kurus across their peril—now you leave the warriors without a vessel and depart to the world of the fathers."

sanskrit: adya prabhṛti saṃkruddhā vyāghrā iva mṛgakṣayam pāṇḍavā bharataśreṣṭha kariṣyanti kurukṣayam
english: "From this day on, enraged like tigers wreaking slaughter among deer, the Pāṇḍavas, O best of the Bharatas, will work the ruin of the Kurus."

sanskrit: adya gāṇḍīvaghoṣasya vīryajñāḥ savyasācinaḥ kuravaḥ saṃtrasiṣyanti vajrapāṇer ivāsurāḥ
english: "Today the Kurus, who know the prowess of Savyasācin, will tremble at the roar of the Gāṇḍīva, as the asuras tremble before the wielder of the thunderbolt."

sanskrit: adya gāṇḍīvamuktānām aśanīnām iva svanaḥ trāsayiṣyati saṃgrāme kurūn anyāṃś ca pārthivān
english: "Today the sound of the shafts loosed from the Gāṇḍīva, like thunderbolts, will strike terror in battle into the Kurus and the other kings as well."

sanskrit: samiddho 'gnir yathā vīra mahājvālo drumān dahet dhārtarāṣṭrān pradhakṣyanti tathā bāṇāḥ kirīṭinaḥ
english: "As a kindled fire with mighty flames burns up the trees, O hero, so will Kirīṭin's arrows consume the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra."

sanskrit: yena yena prasarato vāyvagnī sahitau vane tena tena pradahato bhagavantau yad icchataḥ
english: "Wherever the wind and fire advance together through the forest, there those two mighty lords burn whatever they will."

sanskrit: yādṛśo 'gniḥ samiddho hi tādṛk pārtho na saṃśayaḥ yathā vāyur naravyāghra tathā kṛṣṇo na saṃśayaḥ
english: "As is the kindled fire, such is Pārtha—of that there is no doubt; and as is the wind, O tiger among men, such is Kṛṣṇa—of that no doubt at all."

sanskrit: nadataḥ pāñcajanyasya rasato gāṇḍivasya ca śrutvā sarvāṇi sainyāni trāsaṃ yāsyanti bhārata
english: "Hearing the blare of the Pāñcajanya and the twang of the Gāṇḍīva, all the armies will be seized with terror, O Bhārata."

sanskrit: kapidhvajasya cotpāte rathasyāmitrakarśinaḥ śabdaṃ soḍhuṃ na śakṣyanti tvām ṛte vīra pārthivāḥ
english: "And at the onrush of the ape-bannered chariot of the foe-grinding warrior, none of the kings save you, O hero, will be able to endure its thunder."

sanskrit: ko hy arjunaṃ raṇe yoddhuṃ tvad anyaḥ pārthivo 'rhati yasya divyāni karmāṇi pravadanti manīṣiṇaḥ
english: "For what king but you is fit to fight Arjuna in battle—he whose deeds the wise proclaim to be divine?"

sanskrit: amānuṣaś ca saṃgrāmas tryambakena ca dhīmataḥ tasmāc caiva varaḥ prāpto duṣprāpaś cākṛtātmabhiḥ
english: "More than human was his combat with the three-eyed god, and from him too the wise one won a boon unattainable by men of unperfected souls."

sanskrit: tam adyāhaṃ pāṇḍavaṃ yuddhaśauṇḍam; amṛṣyamāṇo bhavatānuśiṣṭaḥ āśīviṣaṃ dṛṣṭiharaṃ sughoram; iyāṃ puraskṛtya vadhaṃ jayaṃ vā
english: "Today, unable to brook that war-loving son of Pāṇḍu—a venomous serpent, sight-destroying, most dread—and instructed by you, I shall go forth to meet him, setting before me either his death or my own victory."

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tasya lālapyataḥ śrutvā vṛddhaḥ kurupitāmahaḥ deśakālocitaṃ vākyam abravīt prītamānasaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Hearing him lament thus, the aged grandsire of the Kurus, his heart well pleased, spoke words fitting to the place and the hour.

sanskrit: samudra iva sindhūnāṃ jyotiṣām iva bhāskaraḥ satyasya ca yathā santo bījānām iva corvarā
english: "As the ocean is to the rivers, as the sun is to the lights of heaven, as the good are to truth, as fertile soil is to the seeds—"

sanskrit: parjanya iva bhūtānāṃ pratiṣṭhā suhṛdāṃ bhava bāndhavās tvānujīvantu sahasrākṣam ivāmarāḥ
english: "—as the rain-cloud is to living things, so be a stay to your friends. May your kinsmen live under you, as the immortals live under the thousand-eyed one."

sanskrit: svabāhubalavīryeṇa dhārtarāṣṭrapriyaiṣiṇā karṇa rājapuraṃ gatvā kāmbojā nihatās tvayā
english: "By the strength and valor of your own arm, seeking the good of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son, O Karṇa, you went to Rājapura and there slew the Kāmbojas."

sanskrit: girivrajagatāś cāpi nagnajitpramukhā nṛpāḥ ambaṣṭhāś ca videhāś ca gāndhārāś ca jitās tvayā
english: "The kings dwelling at Girivraja, with Nagnajit at their head, and the Ambaṣṭhas, the Videhas, and the Gāndhāras—all were conquered by you."

sanskrit: himavaddurganilayāḥ kirātā raṇakarkaśāḥ duryodhanasya vaśagāḥ kṛtāḥ karṇa tvayā purā
english: "The Kirātas, dwelling in the fastnesses of the Himavat, hardened in war, you, Karṇa, made subject to Duryodhana in days gone by."

sanskrit: tatra tatra ca saṃgrāme duryodhanahitaiṣiṇā bahavaś ca jitā vīrās tvayā karṇa mahaujasā
english: "And in battle here and there, seeking Duryodhana's welfare, many heroes were vanquished by you, O Karṇa of mighty energy."

sanskrit: yathā duryodhanas tāta sajñātikulabāndhavaḥ tathā tvam api sarveṣāṃ kauravāṇāṃ gatir bhava
english: "As Duryodhana is, my son, with his kinsmen, clan, and relations, so be you too a refuge for all the Kauravas."

sanskrit: śivenābhivadāmi tvāṃ gaccha yudhyasva śatrubhiḥ anuśādhi kurūn saṃkhye dhatsva duryodhane jayam
english: "With a blessing I bid you farewell: go, do battle with the foes, lead the Kurus in the fray, and set victory in Duryodhana's hands."

sanskrit: bhavān pautrasamo 'smākaṃ yathā duryodhanas tathā tavāpi dharmataḥ sarve yathā tasya vayaṃ tathā
english: "You are as a grandson to us, even as Duryodhana is; and by dharma we are all yours, just as we are his."

sanskrit: yaunāt saṃbandhakāl loke viśiṣṭaṃ saṃgataṃ satām sadbhiḥ saha naraśreṣṭha pravadanti manīṣiṇaḥ
english: "The fellowship of the good, O best of men, the wise declare to be in this world more excellent than the bond of marriage or of blood—the union of the worthy with the worthy."

sanskrit: sa satyasaṃgaro bhūtvā mamedam iti niścitam kurūṇāṃ pālaya balaṃ yathā duryodhanas tathā
english: "True to your pledge, then, resolved that 'this host is mine,' guard the army of the Kurus, even as Duryodhana would."

sanskrit: iti śrutvā vacaḥ so 'tha caraṇāv abhivādya ca yayau vaikartanaḥ karṇas tūrṇam āyodhanaṃ prati
english: Having heard these words, and having bowed at his feet, Vaikartana Karṇa swiftly went toward the field of battle.

sanskrit: so 'bhivīkṣya naraughāṇāṃ sthānam apratimaṃ mahat vyūḍhapraharaṇoraskaṃ sainyaṃ tat samabṛṃhayat
english: Surveying the vast, matchless station of those throngs of men, he marshaled that army, its breast arrayed with weapons, into fuller strength.

sanskrit: karṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā maheṣvāsaṃ yuddhāya samavasthitam kṣveḍitāsphoṭitaravaiḥ siṃhanādaravair api dhanuḥśabdaiś ca vividhaiḥ kuravaḥ samapūjayan
english: Seeing the great archer Karṇa take his stand for battle, the Kurus honored him with roars and the slapping of arms, with lion-shouts, and with the manifold twanging of bows.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca rathasthaṃ puruṣavyāghraṃ dṛṣṭvā karṇam avasthitam hṛṣṭo duryodhano rājann idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Saṃjaya said: Beholding that tiger among men, Karṇa, stationed and ready in his chariot, Duryodhana, O king, rejoiced and spoke these words.

sanskrit: sanātham idam atyarthaṃ bhavatā pālitaṃ balam manye kiṃ tu samarthaṃ yad dhitaṃ tat saṃpradhāryatām
english: "This army, guarded by you, is now exceedingly well-led, I think. Yet let it be considered well what course is fit and beneficial."

sanskrit: karṇa uvāca brūhi tat puruṣavyāghra tvaṃ hi prājñatamo nṛpa yathā cārthapatiḥ kṛtyaṃ paśyate na tathetaraḥ
english: Karṇa said: "Tell it yourself, O tiger among men, for you, O king, are the wisest; as the master of an affair sees what must be done, no other does so."

sanskrit: te sma sarve tava vacaḥ śrotukāmā nareśvara nānyāyyaṃ hi bhavān vākyaṃ brūyād iti matir mama
english: "We are all eager to hear your word, O lord of men; for you would utter nothing unjust—such is my conviction."

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca bhīṣmaḥ senāpraṇetāsīd vayasā vikrameṇa ca śrutena ca susaṃpannaḥ sarvair yodhaguṇais tathā
english: Duryodhana said: "Bhīṣma was leader of our host, well endowed in years and valor and learning, and in all a warrior's qualities besides."

sanskrit: tenātiyaśasā karṇa ghnatā śatrugaṇān mama suyuddhena daśāhāni pālitāḥ smo mahātmanā
english: "By that most glorious one, O Karṇa, who slew the hosts of my foes, by that great-souled man's good warfare, we were protected for ten days."

sanskrit: tasminn asukaraṃ karma kṛtavaty āsthite divam kaṃ nu senāpraṇetāraṃ manyase tadanantaram
english: "Now that he has done the hard task and ascended to heaven, whom do you deem fit to be leader of the host in his stead?"

sanskrit: na ṛte nāyakaṃ senā muhūrtam api tiṣṭhati āhaveṣv āhavaśreṣṭha netṛhīneva naur jale
english: "Without a leader an army cannot stand even a moment in battle, O best in war, any more than a rudderless ship upon the water."

sanskrit: yathā hy akarṇadhārā nau rathaś cāsārathir yathā draved yatheṣṭaṃ tadvat syād ṛte senāpatiṃ balam
english: "As a ship without a helmsman, or a chariot without a charioteer, would drift whither it would, so would a host be without its commander."

sanskrit: sa bhavān vīkṣya sarveṣu māmakeṣu mahātmasu paśya senāpatiṃ yuktam anu śāṃtanavād iha
english: "Therefore, looking upon all my great-souled men, do you mark out one fit to be commander, next after Śāntanu's son."

sanskrit: yaṃ hi senāpraṇetāraṃ bhavān vakṣyati saṃyuge taṃ vayaṃ sahitāḥ sarve prakariṣyāma māriṣa
english: "For whomever you name as leader of the host in the fight, him shall we all together set up, good sir."

sanskrit: karṇa uvāca sarva eva mahātmāna ime puruṣasattamāḥ senāpatitvam arhanti nātra kāryā vicāraṇā
english: Karṇa said: "All these great-souled men, these best of men, are worthy of the command—herein no debate is needed."

sanskrit: kulasaṃhananajñānair balavikramabuddhibhiḥ yuktāḥ kṛtajñā hrīmanta āhaveṣv anivartinaḥ
english: "Endowed with noble birth, hardihood, and skill, with strength, prowess, and judgment, grateful, full of modesty, never turning back in battle—"

sanskrit: yugapan na tu te śakyāḥ kartuṃ sarve puraḥsarāḥ eka evātra kartavyo yasmin vaiśeṣikā guṇāḥ
english: "—yet they cannot all be made leaders at once. One alone must be chosen here, in whom the special virtues reside."

sanskrit: anyonyaspardhināṃ teṣāṃ yady ekaṃ satkariṣyasi śeṣā vimanaso vyaktaṃ na yotsyante hi bhārata
english: "They vie with one another; if you honor one of them, the rest, downcast, will plainly refuse to fight, O Bhārata."

sanskrit: ayaṃ tu sarvayodhānām ācāryaḥ sthaviro guruḥ yuktaḥ senāpatiḥ kartuṃ droṇaḥ śastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ
english: "But this one—the teacher of all the warriors, the venerable preceptor—is fit to be made commander: Droṇa, foremost of those who bear arms."

sanskrit: ko hi tiṣṭhati durdharṣe droṇe brahmaviduttame senāpatiḥ syād anyo 'smāc chukrāṅgirasadarśanāt
english: "For while the unassailable Droṇa stands—best of the knowers of Brahman, with the insight of Śukra and Aṅgiras—who other than he could be commander?"

sanskrit: na ca sa hy asti te yodhaḥ sarvarājasu bhārata yo droṇaṃ samare yāntaṃ nānuyāsyati saṃyuge
english: "And there is not, among all your kings, a single warrior, O Bhārata, who would not follow Droṇa as he advances into the thick of battle."

sanskrit: eṣa senāpraṇetṝṇām eṣa śastrabhṛtām api eṣa buddhimatāṃ caiva śreṣṭho rājan guruś ca te
english: "He is the best of leaders of hosts, the best of those who bear arms, the best of the wise as well—and he is your preceptor, O king."

sanskrit: evaṃ duryodhanācāryam āśu senāpatiṃ kuru jigīṣanto 'surān saṃkhye kārttikeyam ivāmarāḥ
english: "Therefore, Duryodhana, make the preceptor commander at once, as the immortals, longing to conquer the asuras in battle, made Kārttikeya their own."

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca karṇasya vacanaṃ śrutvā rājā duryodhanas tadā senāmadhyagataṃ droṇam idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Saṃjaya said: Having heard Karṇa's words, King Duryodhana then spoke these words to Droṇa, who stood in the midst of the army.

sanskrit: varṇaśraiṣṭhyāt kulotpattyā śrutena vayasā dhiyā vīryād dākṣyād adhṛṣyatvād arthajñānān nayāj jayāt
english: "By eminence of caste, by birth of family, by learning, by years, by wisdom, by valor, by skill, by invincibility, by knowledge of affairs, by statecraft, by victory—"

sanskrit: tapasā ca kṛtajñatvād vṛddhaḥ sarvaguṇair api yukto bhavatsamo goptā rājñām anyo na vidyate
english: "—and by austerity and by gratitude, you who are aged and endowed with every virtue: among kings there is no other protector your equal."

sanskrit: sa bhavān pātu naḥ sarvān vibudhān iva vāsavaḥ bhavannetrāḥ parāñ jetum icchāmo dvijasattama
english: "So may you guard us all, as Vāsava guards the gods. With you as our guide we long to conquer the foe, O best of the twice-born."

sanskrit: rudrāṇām iva kāpālī vasūnām iva pāvakaḥ kubera iva yakṣāṇāṃ marutām iva vāsavaḥ
english: "As the Skull-bearer among the Rudras, as the Fire among the Vasus, as Kubera among the Yakṣas, as Vāsava among the Maruts—"

sanskrit: vasiṣṭha iva viprāṇāṃ tejasām iva bhāskaraḥ pitṝṇām iva dharmo 'tha ādityānām ivāmburāṭ
english: "—as Vasiṣṭha among the brāhmaṇas, as the sun among the radiant powers, as Dharma among the fathers, as the lord of waters among the Ādityas—"

sanskrit: nakṣatrāṇām iva śaśī ditijānām ivośanāḥ śreṣṭhaḥ senāpraṇetṝṇāṃ sa naḥ senāpatir bhava
english: "—as the moon among the stars, as Uśanas among the sons of Diti—so, best of the leaders of hosts, be you our commander."

sanskrit: akṣauhiṇyo daśaikā ca vaśagāḥ santu te 'nagha tābhiḥ śatrūn prativyūhya jahīndro dānavān iva
english: "Let the eleven akṣauhiṇīs be subject to you, O sinless one; with them array against the foe and slay them, as Indra slew the dānavas."

sanskrit: prayātu no bhavān agre devānām iva pāvakiḥ anuyāsyāmahe tv ājau saurabheyā ivarṣabham
english: "Let you go before us, as the son of Fire goes before the gods; and we shall follow you into battle as bullocks follow the bull."

sanskrit: ugradhanvā maheṣvāso divyaṃ visphārayan dhanuḥ agre bhavantaṃ dṛṣṭvā no nārjunaḥ prasahiṣyate
english: "Fierce-bowed, a great archer, twanging your celestial bow—seeing you at our head, not even Arjuna will withstand us."

sanskrit: dhruvaṃ yudhiṣṭhiraṃ saṃkhye sānubandhaṃ sabāndhavam jeṣyāmi puruṣavyāghra bhavān senāpatir yadi
english: "Surely I shall conquer Yudhiṣṭhira in battle, with his followers and his kinsmen, O tiger among men, if you are our commander."

sanskrit: evam ukte tato droṇe jayety ūcur narādhipāḥ siṃhanādena mahatā harṣayantas tavātmajam
english: When Droṇa had been so addressed, the kings cried out "Victory!" and with a great lion-roar they gladdened your son.

sanskrit: sainikāś ca mudā yuktā vardhayanti dvijottamam duryodhanaṃ puraskṛtya prārthayanto mahad yaśaḥ
english: And the soldiers, filled with joy, acclaimed that best of the twice-born, setting Duryodhana at their head and praying for great glory.

sanskrit: droṇa uvāca vedaṃ ṣaḍaṅgaṃ vedāham arthavidyāṃ ca mānavīm traiyambakam atheṣvastram astrāṇi vividhāni ca
english: Droṇa said: "I know the Veda with its six branches, and the science of statecraft taught by Manu, and the archery of the three-eyed god, and weapons of many kinds."

sanskrit: ye cāpy uktā mayi guṇā bhavadbhir jayakāṅkṣibhiḥ cikīrṣus tān ahaṃ satyān yodhayiṣyāmi pāṇḍavān
english: "And those virtues which you, longing for victory, have named in me—seeking to make them true, I shall do battle with the Pāṇḍavas."

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca sa evam abhyanujñātaś cakre senāpatiṃ tataḥ droṇaṃ tava suto rājan vidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā
english: Saṃjaya said: Granted leave thus, your son then made Droṇa commander of the host, O king, with the rite ordained by precept.
